transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. In photos and in the mirror, one side just looks old and beat-up to me. Other people say they barely see anything, but I see it all the time.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking that area of your face in mirrors or photos?

Yeah. Before work, I’ll stand in the bathroom mirror and turn my face different ways under the light, checking that spot over and over. I rub at it too. If I’m going somewhere, like my sister’s game night, I might pull a hat down low—or just make an excuse not to go if it looks too obvious to me.
When you avoid seeing people, is it mainly because you’re afraid they’ll judge or notice that part of your face?

Yeah. I don’t want people staring at my face or taking pictures where it’ll show. I’ve been late getting out to construction jobs because of it, dodging site photos, and I’ve skipped some family game nights too.
Do you believe for certain that this part of your face looks abnormal to other people?

I mean, I’m pretty sure it does. That patch looks rough and sunken to me—like that side of my face is old and beat-up. People tell me they barely notice it, but when I look in the mirror or see a photo, it’s right there.
Do you ever think it is possible that the problem with your face looks much less noticeable to other people than it does to you?

Maybe, I guess. People keep telling me they barely notice it. But when I see it in the mirror or in a photo, it looks rough and sunken—like that whole side of my face looks old and beat-up. I can’t really stop seeing it.
Do thoughts about that part of your face keep coming into your mind even when you try not to think about it?

Yeah, all the time. I’ll try to focus on something else, but then I catch myself thinking about that patch again—how rough and sunken it looks, especially in mirrors or photos. It feels like that side of my face just looks old and beat-up.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living or that you’d be better off dead because of how your face looks?
I’m not sure what you mean. I know I feel really bothered by how it looks, but I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
If that patch on your face didn’t bother you, would you still feel very anxious in social situations?
I’m not sure. I mean, I think I’d feel a lot less on edge around people if I wasn’t worrying about that patch, but I can’t really separate it out in my head.
Are you also very anxious in social situations when your face is not visible?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m anxious when people can’t see my face.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I know I get pretty upset about my face, but I haven’t really noticed whether I feel depressed most of the day.
Aside from worrying about your face, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
I don’t know, really. I get upset when I’m thinking about my face, but I haven’t noticed feeling sad or down all day otherwise.
When you’re with other people and not thinking about your face, do you still feel afraid that they’ll judge or embarrass you?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to that when I’m not thinking about my face.
Do you pick at that area of your face?
Yeah, sometimes. I’ll rub at the spot, especially when I’m checking it in the bathroom mirror before work. I keep turning my face under different lights to see how obvious it looks.
When you check or rub that area of your face, does it make you feel less anxious, even if only for a little while?

Yeah, for a little bit, I guess. If I keep checking it under the lights and rub at it, I feel like I can tell how bad it looks. But then before work or my sister’s game night, I’ll check again and again. Sometimes I just pull my hat down low, or make an excuse not to go if it looks too obvious.
Do you check or rub that area only because of how it looks?

Mostly, yeah. I’m checking to see how obvious that spot looks. Before work or my sister’s game night, I’ll keep looking in the bathroom mirror, turn my face under different lights, rub at it. If it looks bad, I might pull my hat down low or just make an excuse not to go.
Are these repeated thoughts and checking behaviors only about that spot on your face?

No, it’s really that patch. I see it in the mirror and in photos—it looks rough and sunken, like that side of my face is old and beat-up. Other people say they barely notice it, but I can’t stop seeing it.
In social situations where you are not worried about that spot on your face, do you still feel afraid that people will judge you?
I’m not sure. Most of the time if I’m worried people are looking at me, it’s because of that spot. I haven’t really noticed being afraid of judgment when it’s not on my mind.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying that there is something wrong with how your face looks, even though other people say they barely notice it?

Yeah. I keep seeing that rough, sunken patch—especially in mirrors or photos. It makes that side of my face look old and beat-up to me. People tell me they barely notice it, but I just can’t seem to let it go.
On a typical day, do you spend more than an hour thinking about that spot on your face?

Yeah, more than an hour. I keep looking at it in mirrors or photos and thinking about how rough and sunken it looks, like that side of my face is old and beat-up. Even when people tell me they barely see it, I can’t stop focusing on it.
When your face is completely covered and no one can see that spot, do you still feel very anxious around people?

If it’s completely covered, I’m less worried about people seeing it. But I still keep thinking about how it looks underneath—the rough, sunken patch. Even though people say they hardly notice it, I can’t really get it out of my head.
